issues.title: Agent Output Contract
issues.dod: arm emits one structured-output contract on one channel, every agent-facing command conforms to it, and a deterministic gate blocks a new or modified command from drifting off it. Measured: arm list falls from ~86k to ~22k estimated tokens.
acceptance: arm validate passes with no errors

issues.title: Define and expand the Agent Output Contract
issues.dod: The contract is written down and its implementation exists alongside the current output paths, with nothing migrated yet and make check green. This is the expand half of an expand-contract sequence: 30 files under cmd/armature touch format, so no single vertical slice can migrate them all green.
acceptance: arm validate passes with no errors

issues.title: Contract definition: ADR 0017 and the normative output spec
notes: Glossary terms Agent Output Contract, Protocol Output and Artifact Output, and the Surface amendment covering output shape, landed with the decision record. This task adds the ADR and the normative spec section.

ADR 0017 covers one decision with three faces: single channel (stdout, errors included, stderr diagnostics-only), uniform envelope including single-item responses, and explicit Protocol Output and mode-sensitive Artifact Output carve-outs. It also records that the contract is deliberately unversioned pre-1.0 with TOPTIER-S6-T3 as the freeze point, and cites AXI as prior art rather than a conformed-to standard.
issues.dod: ADR 0017 records the Agent Output Contract: single channel, uniform envelope {count, payload[], help[]}, and the Protocol Output and Artifact Output carve-outs. docs/design/agent-output-contract.md gains a normative section stating the envelope, channel, default list schema, help[] rules, empty-state rules and mode-sensitive classification precisely enough for a lint to be written against it. The implementation plan carries those classifications into the downstream helper, lint and census tasks.
acceptance: ADR 0017 exists and is referenced from docs/design/agent-output-contract.md

issues.title: Envelope and channel helpers, added alongside existing output
notes: Expand step. Intentionally horizontal: it delivers no user-visible change, and exists so each later command migration can land green on its own.

Deliberately does not touch main.go or helpers.go. Because classification defaults to agent-facing, only the single Protocol Output command needs an explicit opt-out, so no root-command edit is required and this task stays disjoint from LNGHZN-S6-T1 and NXTTN-S4-T1.
issues.dod: internal/output gains an envelope constructor producing {count, <payload>[], help[]} and a writer that emits it to stdout, both usable without touching existing output paths. Commands carry an agent-facing / Protocol Output classification that defaults to agent-facing, so a new command cannot silently opt out; harness-hook declares itself the sole Protocol Output. No command is migrated in this task and existing output is byte-identical.

issues.title: Mode-sensitive Artifact Output classification
issues.scope: internal/output/classify.go, internal/output/classify_test.go, cmd/armature/review.go, cmd/armature/review_test.go, cmd/armature/cmd_completion.go, cmd/armature/cmd_completion_test.go, cmd/armature/decompose.go, cmd/armature/cmd_extra_test.go
notes: Remediation added after AOC-S1-T2 completed with only agent-facing and Protocol Output classifications. Preserve that history; this task extends the classifier rather than retroactively claiming T2 delivered the third class.

Artifact Output applies to review prepare with --output unset, completion, and dag apply --schema|--example. Each mark cites its governing schema or consumer; review prepare --output <file> and ordinary dag apply remain agent-facing.
issues.dod: The output classifier adds explicit, cited Artifact Output alongside agent-facing and Protocol Output. Classification is mode-sensitive: the three normative artifact modes opt out, while other modes of the same commands remain agent-facing. Existing output bytes do not change.

issues.title: Migrate commands to the Agent Output Contract
issues.dod: Every agent-facing command emits the contract envelope on stdout. Each task is a vertical slice verifiable on its own; the batches are sized by blast radius so make check stays green between them.
acceptance: arm validate passes with no errors

issues.title: arm list conforms to the contract
notes: Carries the measured saving: 342,560 bytes to roughly 89,000 on a 738-issue graph.
--group is currently accepted and silently inert in non-TTY while two deployed skills instruct agents to use it.

Owns its own docs/commands.md lines per E13: stories deliver vertical slices, not horizontal layers. Because only one task may own a file at a time, the S2 migrations run as a chain rather than a parallel wave.
issues.dod: arm list emits {count, issues[], help[]} on stdout with a default row of id, type, status, title. outcome is omitted from list output entirely rather than truncated, because the detail view already exists. count is the true total and the list is not capped. help[] trails the list pointing at arm show for detail. --group produces grouped structured output rather than being silently ignored. An empty result is a definitive empty state.

issues.title: arm ready conforms to the contract

issues.dod: arm ready emits {count, issues[], help[]} on stdout. Expired claims move off stderr into the envelope as a named field rather than a separate stderr array, closing the case where an agent running 2>/dev/null silently loses them. An empty ready queue is a definitive empty state carrying the zero and its context, not a bare []. The --waves shape is folded into the same envelope.

issues.dod: arm show honours the structured contract instead of falling through to human prose, emitting the envelope on stdout. outcome and other large text fields are truncated by default with the total size stated and a --full escape hatch offered only when content was actually truncated. This is the detail view that arm list's help[] directs agents to, so the truncation limit is chosen to cover the common case in one call.

notes: One task rather than three because all three changes touch the root command and would otherwise collide on scope during wave planning.

issues.title: Retire legacy output and enforce the contract
issues.dod: The old output paths are gone and two deterministic gates hold the contract: byte budgets for size and a shape lint for conformance. A new or modified CLI command cannot ship non-conforming output without failing make check. This is the contract half of the expand-contract sequence.

issues.title: Retire the legacy output paths
notes: Contract step: safe only once no caller remains.

Scoped to internal/output only. By the time every command has migrated there is no cmd/ caller of the legacy path left to clean up, and keeping cmd/** out of scope keeps this task from tripping E13 against the census task.
issues.dod: The pre-contract output writers and the jsonErrorPayload path are deleted, leaving exactly one way to emit structured output. No caller remains on the old form and the deletion is a pure subtraction with no behaviour change.

issues.title: Price dynamic structured payloads in context-report
notes: NXTTN-S3 and NXTTN-S3-T1 currently exclude dynamic artifacts as a known limitation; this task closes that gap and both DoDs should be amended to drop the exclusion.
Prices must be measured against checked-in fixtures, not a live repo, or the gate's output varies with how many issues the developer happens to have.
issues.dod: internal/contextreport prices structured command payloads using the same bytes/4 convention as static artifacts, measured against a checked-in fixture graph so the number is reproducible. Dynamic payloads join the existing budgets file and shrink-only ratchet, with initial values seeded at or above current measured size so the gate starts green. NXTTN-S3 and NXTTN-S3-T1 have their dynamic-artifacts-out-of-scope clause removed.

issues.title: Shape lint enumerated from the cobra command tree
notes: This is the guardrail. The enumeration source must be the command tree itself: a fixture list maintained by hand is a gate over the commands somebody remembered to fixture, which is the hole this task exists to close.

Conformance means: envelope present, payload key named, count present on collections, help[] present where required, nothing written to stderr, definitive empty state. Protocol Output and Artifact Output are exempt only through explicit classification; mode-sensitive Artifact Output commands fixture both their artifact and agent-facing modes.
issues.dod: A lint enumerates every registered cobra command mode. Each agent-facing mode requires a conforming golden; a missing fixture fails make check. Protocol Output and Artifact Output modes are exempt only by explicit classification, never by name. Each Artifact Output mode is checked against its cited foreign shape, while other modes of the same command require envelope fixtures.

issues.title: Census coverage for output shape and command classification
notes: census-drift-check already compares CLI commands and flags bidirectionally; this extends the same mechanism to the surfaces the Surface glossary amendment brought into scope.
issues.dod: surface-census.md records structured shape and agent-facing / Protocol Output / Artifact Output classification per command mode, including selecting flags and cited shape for Artifact modes. census-drift-check compares rows with code bidirectionally, failing changed classifications or flags without rows and phantom rows without code. The self-test covers the new sections.

issues.title: ADR 0019: park TOON with a re-entry criterion
notes: Gets its own ADR rather than a consequences note so the re-entry criterion stays findable; a park buried in another decision quietly becomes a purge, which is what ADR 0010 exists to prevent.

Measured basis: the minimal schema captures roughly 68 percent of available saving and TOON roughly 30 percent of what remains. Costs that made it a park: no Go encoder exists, quoting is load-bearing given 98 of 738 titles contain commas, and it would be a new wire format pinned by embed-examples and every skill example.
issues.dod: ADR 0019 records TOON as parked, not rejected, using the park-not-purge vocabulary of ADR 0010. It states the measured basis and the costs that made it a park, and its re-entry criterion is expressed in the units make context-report now emits so it can be evaluated mechanically rather than re-argued.
acceptance: ADR 0019 exists with an explicit re-entry criterion in context-report units

issues.title: Payload-keyed op idempotency
notes: Independent of the output work; runs in parallel.
issues.dod: Re-issuing a mutation that cannot change materialized state is a no-op at exit 0 that appends nothing, while a repeat carrying new information is recorded as an amendment. Measured against the current 9,172-op corpus: suppresses 14 true duplicates, preserves all 29 amendments.
acceptance: arm validate passes with no errors

issues.title: Payload-keyed transition idempotency and ADR 0018
notes: Evidence from replaying .armature/ops: 43 same-status transitions split into 29 amendments and 14 true duplicates. LNGHZN-S9-T2 reached done seven times with a different, richer outcome each time; suppressing by status alone would have frozen its outcome at the first report and lost the final audit correction.
ORCH-RUNTIME-V1-T3 fired six byte-identical empty-outcome done transitions in 15 minutes; that is the noise this suppresses, and it is 0.153 percent of the whole log.
issues.dod: A mutation whose payload is byte-identical to the issue's current recorded state is a no-op: exit 0, nothing appended, said explicitly rather than erroring. A same-status mutation carrying a changed payload is appended as an amendment at exit 0. ADR 0018 records why idempotency is keyed on payload rather than status, and why declining to append an op that cannot change materialized state does not violate I2.

issues.title: Dogfood finding: worker thrash on repeated identical done reports
notes: Q9b decided suppressed duplicates leave no durable trace, because a counter on an existing op would rewrite history and race under I3. The signal belongs in the dogfood corpus instead.
issues.dod: A raw dogfood finding records the worker-thrash pattern with its evidence: ORCH-RUNTIME-V1-T3 emitting six byte-identical empty-outcome done transitions inside 15 minutes, plus the corpus-wide rate of 14 true duplicates across 1,367 transition ops. The finding names the harness behaviour as the defect rather than the ops log, so that once payload-keyed idempotency suppresses the ops, the underlying loop is still visible as a tracked concern.
acceptance: Finding file exists under docs/dogfood/findings/raw/ following the documented naming convention
